newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court finds Germany late to enact residency rules.
newsitem.headline: Court finds Germany late to enact residency rules.

text.p: The European Court of Justice found on Thursday that Germany was late in enacting Community rules on residency for retired self-employed workers.

Germany argued the European Commission's claims were unfounded because Community law could be relied on directly by the persons covered, there was no ambiguity in the German law, and the competent national authorities knew how to apply the Community law.

The German government argued that a national law making reference to Community law could satisfy the requirement of legal clarity, allowing citizens access to Official Journal citations. Additionally, Germany argued that in a case such as this, where the directives at issue are self-executing and individuals can fully assess their rights, there is no need for direct transposition.
The court disagreed, and said that publication in the OJ "cannot relieve member states of the obligatiion to adopt the necessary implementing measures."

"The right of persons to rely in law on a directive against a member state in specific circumstances is no more than a minimum guarantee, arising from the binding nature of the obligation imposed on the member states by the...treaty, which cannot justify a member state's absolving itself from taking in due time implementing measures sufficient to meet the purpose of each directive," the court said.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: German)
"Failure of a member state to fulfil an obligation - Right of residence - Council directives 90/364/EEC and 90/365/EEC"

application for a declaration that, by not adopting within the prescribed period, or by not communicating to the Commission forthwith, the laws, regulations, and administrative provisions necessary for transposing into national law Council directive 90/365/EEC of 28 June 1990 on the right of residence for employees and self-employed persons who have ceased their occupational activity (OJ 1990 L 180, p. 28) and Council directive 90/364/EEC of 28 June 1990 on the right of residence (OJ 1990 L 180, p. 26), the Federal Republic of Germany has failed its obligations under the EC Treaty

1. Declares that, by not adopting within the prescribed period, or by not communicating to the Commission forthwith, the laws, regulations, and administrative provisions necessary for transposing into national law Council directive 90/365/EEC of 28 June 1990 on the right of residence for employees and self-employed persons who have ceased their occupational activity and Council directive 90/364/EEC of 28 June 1990 on the right of residence, the Federal Republic of Germany has failed its obligations under article 5 of those two directives.
2. Orders the Federal Republic of Germany to pay the costs.
